Header banner for /collections/acetyl-hexapeptide-8.

SOURCE: banner library, acetyl-hexapeptide-8-serum--J-body-and-face-right nbp_pro_01
(6336x2688, 2.36:1 — far larger than the other library frames, so the extender scales
it to the 848px working height first). Label checked at 100%: Skingenetix / ACETYL
HEXAPEPTIDE-8 / ANTI-WRINKLE all correct; the line below is behind her fingers, which
is occlusion in the shot rather than a rendering fault.

CANVAS EXTENDED, not cropped, to 3750x848 (4.42:1) — past the 4.36:1 that a 100vw x
440px box reaches at a 1920 viewport, so the full height survives there. The header
keeps the theme's standard sm height like every other collection page.

Her shoulder TOUCHES the left edge at y=428 and the line steepens as it recedes
(391 at x=120, 428 at x=0). It is not extended across the new canvas — it leaves
frame the way it physically would, curving down and falling out of the key light,
gone within ~260px. Backdrop measures mean 30.1, max 35, sd 1.3 over rows 0-380 and
cols 0-300, so the weave is mirror-tiled from there.

TEXT SITS TOP-LEFT, not centre-left: her shoulder crosses the middle, leaving only
435px of clear zone at centre height against 858px across the top, and the title
needs 654px to stay on one line.

ROUND 2 FRAME, REPLACING THE LIBRARY ORIGINAL. Malcolm: the product text was not showing clearly and the liquid inside the frosted bottle should be transparent rather than white. Both traced to the banner-library brief, which showed only three of the label's seven elements and described the contents as an opaque fill. The rebuild quotes the full label verbatim with the weight of every line and describes the serum as a liquid. On the chosen frame all seven read at native pixels: Skingenetix / ACETYL HEXAPEPTIDE-8 / ANTI-WRINKLE SERUM / PREMIUM FORMULA / 10% ACETYL HEXAPEPTIDE-8 | 30ML.

SCATTER, NOT TILE, AND MEASURED BOTH WAYS. Mirror-tiling this backdrop left a seam: the largest step in the extension's smoothed column profile landed exactly on the 690px tile width. Switching to scattered grain drops the worst residual step to 0.05 levels, well under anything an eye resolves. Worth recording that the first metric used - raw column-to-column difference - said scatter was WORSE, because random grain raises per-pixel variance; it was the wrong test. A seam is a step in the SMOOTHED profile, and that is what had to be measured.
